notes: Embrace Uncertainty (Alday, Kliegl and Bates), ch. Large-scale designed experiments (largescaledesigned.qmd at 08f020d7): English Lexicon Project lexical decision trials (Balota et al. 2007), subjects and items incompletely crossed; elm01 fits 1000 / rt ~ 1 + isword * wrdlen + (1 | item) + (1 | subj) on the trials with non-missing acc and 200 <= rt <= 3000 (elm02 also drops subjects under 80% accuracy); MixedModelsDatasets.jl docs/src/datasets.md (36eaaacb, sha256 equal to the pin) give the same model. isword (word or nonword) and wrdlen are joined from ELP_ldt_item, but the chapter derives both from this table: wrdlen is the item's length and isword = isodd.(eachindex(byitem.item)), since the items come in word-nonword pairs in the level order. The formula writes them as expressions with the chapter's codings, isword effects-coded (+1 for words) and wrdlen centered at 8. seq is the trial number; acc is row 2's response. Hand check #162: the formula takes the derived word status and its interaction with length, against the reading and its ruling (a term of another file has no column): the parity of the item's level equals ELP_ldt_item's isword, and nchar its wrdlen, on all 80,962 items. covariates and interactions stay blank, against the outside check's item, since both terms are expressions of the grouping factor item (no column: the formula only); as.integer(item) follows the Arrow file's level order.
